title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

providers.name: ServiceNow
providers.scope_notes: Release/plugin dependent. API key/HMAC requires com.glide.tokenbased_auth and API-specific policy. Documentation reviewed is Brazil.

controls.name: REST API access policy
controls.what: Per REST API (or globally), lists the inbound authentication profiles allowed, so unlisted credential types such as Basic are refused.
controls.setting: All > System Web Services > REST API Access Policies (map Inbound Authentication Profiles)
controls.quote: Create an API access policy and map an authentication profile to restrict the authentication type for a REST API.

controls.name: API access policy with adaptive authentication filter criteria (IP)
controls.what: An access policy can combine an allowed auth type with filter criteria such as an IP range; other auth types or IPs are denied.
controls.setting: REST API Access Policies + Adaptive Authentication filter criteria
controls.quote: allows only OAuth 2.0 authentication type from a specified range of IP addresses

controls.name: Adaptive authentication policies
controls.what: Allows or denies authentication by IP address, role or group, including for inbound REST API requests.
controls.setting: All > Adaptive Authentication > Authentication Policies / Filter Criteria
controls.quote: You can use the filter criteria of adaptive authentication framework to restrict access to inbound ServiceNow REST APIs.

controls.name: IP Address Access Control
controls.what: Instance-wide allow/deny IP rules for inbound traffic regardless of credential type.
controls.setting: All > System Security > IP Address Access Control (plugin com.snc.ipauthenticator)
controls.quote: Deny: Any IP address in this range cannot interact with this instance unless it is listed in an Allow rule.

controls.name: OIDC provider for third-party ID tokens (Active, audience, user claim, JTI)
controls.what: Third-party ID tokens are accepted only via an active OIDC provider record that pins the audience, maps a user claim and can verify JTI.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > New > Configure an OIDC provider to verify ID tokens (or Machine Identity Console > Inbound integrations)
controls.quote: This value should be the same as the value of the aud claim in the JWT token.

controls.name: Enforce Token Restrictions (OIDC provider)
controls.what: Third-party ID tokens work only on APIs whose access policy enables the ID token authentication profile.
controls.setting: OIDC provider record > Enforce Token Restrictions
controls.quote: Select this option to allow only tokens used with APIs set to enable the authentication profile.

controls_unknown: Which authentication types the default Global REST API policy allows; the Brazil page names the Global Blocking Policy but does not list them.

authentication.summary: Basic username/password; API key/HMAC via plugin; OAuth bearer including code + PKCE, client credentials and Third-Party ID Token Flow.

federation.details: Inbound Third-Party ID Token Flow trusts external providers such as Entra or Okta, subject to configured trust.

ip_restriction.boundary: REST API access policies can allow only selected authentication types and source IP ranges.

lifetime.summary: External IdP token presented directly; lifetime set by the external IdP

renewal.summary: The client gets a fresh token from the external IdP; renewal follows the IdP's token and session policy.

administration.summary: Roles/ACLs, REST auth scopes, API access policies and OAuth client restrictions. Enable token restrictions to associate tokens with permitted APIs.
administration.conditions: Release/plugin dependent. API key/HMAC requires com.glide.tokenbased_auth and API-specific policy. Documentation reviewed is Brazil.

sso.details: The credential is an ID token issued by the org's external OIDC IdP and accepted through the Multi-Provider SSO option.

sso.ui: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > New > Configure an OIDC provider to verify ID tokens (User Claim / User Field map the token to a sys_user); MFA is enforced at the external IdP

expiry.ui: Lifetime is set in the external IdP; ServiceNow allows Clock Skew (default 300s) on the OIDC provider record under System OAuth > Application Registry

reads.ui: All > System Logs > Transactions; filter Created by = the integration user, then URL (e.g. the REST path called)

token_format.notes: External OIDC ID token (JWT) verified against the provider's metadata/keys.

log_sources.name: Transaction log (System Logs > Transactions)
log_sources.notes: Records requests with Created by, URL, IP address, HTTP Response Code. Retention not stated in docs.

log_sources.name: oauth_credential table
log_sources.notes: Tokens issued after the ID token is accepted.

anomaly_cues: Requests mapped to users who have no activity at the external IdP
Auto-provisioned sys_user records appearing right after ID token use
Calls from IPs outside the calling app's hosts

containment.steps: Disable the OIDC provider / third-party ID token integration; revoke issued tokens in Manage Tokens or via oauth_revoke_token.do; revoke the upstream IdP session.
containment.notes: Upstream ID token revocation does not reach tokens ServiceNow already issued.

sample_query.query: System Logs > Transactions: Created by = idp.mapped.user ^ Created in Last 7 days ^ IP address NOT IN <known integration egress IPs>
sample_query.purpose: Review API activity of a user mapped from an external ID token

calls.call: POST /oauth_token.do (external OIDC provider ID token) -> REST call with mapped session
calls.reveals: Validates a third-party OIDC ID token (aud=client_id) and maps it to a ServiceNow user for inbound API access
calls.scope: OIDC provider config; mapped user's roles
calls.log_notes: The resulting authenticated inbound request is logged as a transaction (Created by = mapped user, URL, IP)

calls.reveals: The mapped user's own record and role summary; confirms identity mapped from the ID token
calls.log_notes: Logged as REST transaction with mapped user

calls.reveals: Table inventory for the mapped user's permissions
calls.log_notes: GET logged with URL and user

calls.reveals: Bulk record data from readable tables; offset paging
calls.log_notes: Each Table API GET logged; retention ~56 days default
